gen-fs-styro-gf-miriam-libre: Styro crowds its letters together with a retro, commanding hush. Miriam Libre sits below in a plain sans, its wire-thin strokes and open s letting the tight heading breathe.
gen-fs-styro-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Mochiy Pop P One reads wide and spacious, every letter set apart with a compass-drawn smoothness. Styro above it is the opposite, tightly packed and carrying a low, retro punch that the body never tries to match.
gen-fs-styro-gf-montserrat-alternates: Styro packs its letters so tightly that the e and c nearly close up, giving it a retro, commanding look. And Montserrat Alternates opens everything back out, its c wide like a bent paperclip.
gen-fs-styro-gf-montserrat-underline: Commanding up top, Styro presses its letters shut, while Montserrat Underline keeps every counter open and every stroke a single width. Reading it would feel steady, unhurried.
gen-fs-styro-gf-mozilla-headline: Styro's letters are pressed so close they nearly crowd one another, a retro look with real authority. But Mozilla Headline is big-bodied sans with a splayed c terminal, and that open friendliness is what sets the pair apart.
gen-fs-styro-gf-mozilla-text: Styro brings a retro, commanding look with its tightly crowded letters, set against the flared terminals of Mozilla Text. Its tall lowercase would read dense and confident.
gen-fs-styro-gf-nata-sans: Crowded letters with barely any gap in the e and c make Styro instantly retro and forceful. Nata Sans loosens things with a big central band and wide, open curves, drawn with technical-pen steadiness.
gen-fs-styro-gf-nobile: Nobile keeps its lowercase close to the capitals, with open mouths like a chalk arc left unjoined. Nobile does the quiet, careful work of text, while Styro, retro and tightly packed, handles the loud part.
gen-fs-styro-gf-nokora: Approachable and clean, Nokora lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, with an s that never tightens. Styro, retro and tightly packed, sits against it with real force.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic reads modern and welcoming, with a gap in the c and capitals barely above the lowercase. Against Styro's crowded retro letters, a longer passage would feel like stepping outside.
